match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the traditional view of both business and government: the government enterprises card covers ownership of public businesses, and the rational decision making card covers only consumers and firms, not government's aim of maximising living standards.

draft.title: The traditional view of business and government
card: Traditional economics assumes a business aims to maximise profit. Profit is total revenue minus total costs.
Traditional economics assumes government aims to maximise the living standards of the community, not to make a profit.
Government pursues this aim in three ways: stabilising the economy, improving efficiency and redistributing income.
Stabilising means working to keep growth steady, prices stable and jobs available. Redistributing means moving income from some households to others, so that the gap between rich and poor is smaller.
draft.remember: Business aims for the most profit. Government aims for the highest living standards for the community.

a.q: Which statement best describes the traditional view of the main aim of a business?
opts: To maximise the gap between its revenue and its costs
To maximise the number of workers it employs
To maximise the living standards of its community
To maximise the sales it makes in each year
a.why: The traditional view says a business seeks the most profit, which is revenue minus costs. Sales matter only as one part of revenue, and a business can sell a lot and still make a poor profit.
a.clue: Think about what is left after costs are paid.

b.q: The Victorian Government raises the income tax paid by high earners and uses it to fund payments for low income families. Which government role does this show?
opts: Redistributing income
Stabilising the economy
Maximising its own profit
Maximising business profit
b.why: Moving income from high earners to low income families is redistribution. It is not stabilising, which is about steady growth, stable prices and jobs. Government does not aim for profit under the traditional view.
b.clue: Who pays the money, and who receives it?

a.best: To maximise the gap between its revenue and its costs

problems.detail: In Australia, income tax is set and collected by the Commonwealth (federal) Government, not a state government. The Victorian Government cannot raise the income tax paid by high earners, so the scenario should name the Australian Government instead.

check.summary: Question b wrongly says the Victorian Government raises income tax; only the federal Government levies income tax in Australia, so the scenario should name the Australian Government. The rest of the point is accurate.
